title: G-SIR: Gaussian Semantic Inverse Rendering for Scaling Open-Vocabulary 3-D Understanding to City-Scale Scenes
content: Integrating open-vocabulary semantics into explicit 3-D representations is essential for embodied agents to interpret unseen concepts, yet scaling such representations to city-scale scenes remains challenging. The dominant neural distillation paradigm suffers from neural spectral bias, which suppresses high-frequency semantic boundaries, and costly iterative optimization over large 3-D representations. We present Gaussian semantic inverse rendering (G-SIR), which recasts semantic lifting as a constrained inverse problem with analytical tractability. Built on surface-aligned 2-D Gaussian splatting (2DGS), G-SIR comprises four sequential stages: 1) geometry-informed feature lifting (G-LIFT) extracts dense CLIP-based semantic supervision; 2) Anchor-based projection with manifold optimization (AP-MO) formulates a similarity-preserving projection using scene-specific text anchors; 3) R-SIR iteratively optimizes the projection on the Stiefel manifold; and 4) closed-form solving performs regularized per-Gaussian semantic assignment without iterative semantic-field optimization. This formulation avoids iterative per-Gaussian neural semantic fitting while improving semantic boundary fidelity. On LERF-Mask, G-SIR achieves the best mean intersection over union (mIoU) and mean boundary IoU (mBIoU) across all three evaluated scenes. On MatrixCity and UrbanScene3D, where pixel-level semantic ground truth is unavailable, experiments provide qualitative semantic evidence together with quantitative efficiency evaluation. UrbanScene3D further provides qualitative evidence of cross-scene semantic generalization across related scenes under scene-specific fitting. G-SIR completes semantic embedding in 15 and 40 min on MatrixCity and UrbanScene3D, respectively, demonstrating practical scalability to city-scale scenes.
author: Di Wu, Wenshuai Yu, Yang Liu, Wenyu Jiang, Yuansheng Hua, Jiasong Zhu

title: Physically Constrained Machine Learning Retrieval of Turbulence Dissipation Rate From Radar Wind Profiler
content: Atmospheric turbulence dissipation rate ( $\varepsilon $ ) is a key parameter for understanding boundary-layer turbulence and its impacts on atmospheric processes. Machine learning (ML) techniques have been applied to retrieve  $\varepsilon $  from radar wind profiler (RWP) observations, but their inherently data-driven nature and strong dependence on turbulent samples lead to overestimation under weak-turbulence conditions, limiting their operational applicability. To address this limitation, this study proposes a physically constrained random forest (RF) framework for retrieving  $\varepsilon $  from RWP observations. The method integrates physical knowledge of boundary-layer turbulence into the RF retrieval through a two-step correction strategy, consisting of a boundary constraint to suppress physically implausible estimates under weak turbulence and an empirical scaling adjustment to enhance sensitivity in low turbulence regimes. The proposed approach is evaluated using one year of the RWP and sonic anemometer measurements at 160 and 320 m at the Shenzhen Shiyan site in Southern China. Results show that the proposed correction improves retrieval performance, increasing the correlation coefficient with in situ measurements from 0.67 to 0.78 and reducing the mean absolute error (MAE) across different turbulence intensities, atmospheric conditions, and seasons. The corrected retrievals reproduce realistic diurnal variations of  $\varepsilon $ , with enhanced daytime turbulence and higher values under clear-sky conditions compared with cloudy periods. These findings provide an effective approach for estimating  $\varepsilon $  from RWP observations, and support the use of RWP for long-term and operational investigations of boundary-layer turbulence.
author: Xin Ma, Boming Liu, Jianping Guo, Zhe Tong, Honglong Yang, Yingying Ma, Wei Gong

title: A Structural Knowledge-Guided Deep Learning for Retrieving Precipitable Water Vapor From Satellite Remote Sensing Observations
content: Near-infrared (NIR) satellite remote sensing provides global precipitable water vapor (PWV) observations at ~1-km spatial resolution; however, its applicability is severely constrained under cloudy-sky conditions, where a substantial proportion of retrievals become unusable due to cloud contamination. To address this limitation, this study proposes a structural knowledge-guided deep learning (SKDL) framework for satellite-based PWV retrieval with enhanced accuracy and spatial continuity. The framework incorporates structural knowledge learned from boosting models into a deep neural network (DNN) via a knowledge distillation mechanism, thereby improving the representation of complex, nonlinear feature interactions. Furthermore, cloud properties are explicitly introduced as new variables to account for cloud-induced radiative transfer effects. The proposed method is evaluated against ERA5 reanalysis and global navigation satellite system (GNSS) observations. ERA5-based spatial validation shows that SKDL-LightGBM (SKDL-LGB) achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.6 mm and a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.90. GNSS-based station validation further indicates that SKDL-LGB) attains a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.15 mm under all-weather conditions, outperforming standalone boosting and deep learning models. These findings demonstrate that integrating distilled structural knowledge and cloud information substantially improves NIR-based PWV retrieval performance, particularly in cloudy-sky conditions. The proposed framework offers a robust and scalable solution for generating high-accuracy, spatially continuous PWV products.
author: Xiuguang Yao, Wenjie Peng, Qi Zhang, Xiongwei Ma, Yuqing Liu, Chaoqian Xu, Yibin Yao, Lin He, Xiaoning Zhang, Jianxun Ding, Meihao Yang

title: Balancing Consistency and Generalization via Cross-Sample Memory Bank for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
content: Change detection (CD) is a fundamental task in remote sensing image analysis, aiming to identify changes between images acquired at different times. For CD, it is critical to learn the consistent features of unchanged regions across multitemporal images. However, forcing consistent features also impacts the representation of diverse scenarios, resulting in decayed generalization capability. In this article, we simultaneously consider the unchanged consistency and cross-scene generalization and propose a constraint and memory network (C-MNet). First, a dual-branch backbone integrating SAM2 and VMamba is constructed to model both spatial and cross-temporal dependencies simultaneously for better capturing the consistency. Then a mask-guided dual-temporal reconstruction module is designed which enforces cross-temporal reconstruction consistency on unchanged areas and enables the network to explicitly learn temporal invariance. However, consistency-driven reconstruction tends to suppress feature diversity in different scenarios, biasing the model toward dominant land-cover patterns. To overcome this limitation, we further design a cross-sample Memory Bank mechanism that stores stable unchanged features and serves as a historical reference during training. C-MNet effectively balances consistency constraints and feature diversity, leading to improved recognition capability of changed regions and cross-scene generalization. The code of this work can be found on https://github.com/4043-lab/Change-detection
author: Xia Zhang, Jinyu Han, Jia Liu, Wenhua Zhang, Fang Liu, Liang Xiao

title: ASG-SAM: Anisotropic Spectral Gating and Multigranularity Decoding for SAM-Based Infrared Small Target Segmentation
content: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) remains challenging due to the extremely small spatial support, weak texture, low target-background contrast, and severe clutter interference. Although the Segment Anything Model (SAM) provides strong promptable segmentation ability, its direct adaptation to IRSTD is still limited. Generic Cartesian feature aggregation is not well matched to the point-spread characteristics of infrared small targets, while fragile target cues are easily diluted during deep semantic propagation. To address these issues, this article proposes anisotropic spectral gating (ASG)-SAM, a physics-aware SAM adaptation framework for infrared small target segmentation. In particular, an ASG module is introduced as a joint radial-angular spectral gate parameterized in the polar frequency domain, improving the compatibility between feature aggregation and point-spread target characteristics. In addition, a difference-of-Gaussians adaptive multigranularity decoder (DoG-AMGD) is designed to recycle intermediate vision transformer (ViT) features and adaptively fuse difference-of-Gaussian (DoG)-style differential cues across multiple granularities, thereby recovering high-frequency target details while suppressing clutter-induced responses. Extensive experiments on three public IRSTD benchmarks, including IRSTD-1K, NUAA-SIRST, and IRSTDID-SKY, demonstrate that ASG-SAM achieves state-of-the-art segmentation performance. Moreover, applying ASG to different SAM variants consistently brings substantial improvements, showing its general effectiveness for adapting promptable segmentation models to infrared small target scenarios. Ablation studies and feature visualizations further verify the complementary effectiveness and interpretability of ASG and DoG-AMGD.
author: Riyao Chen, Mingchao Yang, Zehao Wu, Tianming Xie, Wenxiong Kang

title: HydroDrone: A Circular External-Looking UAV-SAR Campaign for Short-Term Temporal Decorrelation Characterization
content: This article presents the HydroDrone campaign, a dedicated uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) experiment designed to characterize short-term temporal decorrelation over vegetated scenes. The system employs a C-band frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar mounted on a multirotor UAV, performing repeated circular external-looking acquisitions over a chosen test site. This configuration enables the generation of dense interferometric stacks with temporal baselines ranging from tens of seconds to several hours. This work derives the specific mathematical framework for the computation of along-track wavenumbers and azimuth resolution in circular external-looking geometries, highlighting the fundamental differences with respect to standard linear trajectories. To compensate for residual trajectory errors arising from navigation uncertainties, a multiaperture interferometric trajectory compensation algorithm is introduced and applied across the stack. Preliminary results from a single campaign day are presented, including interferometric phase and coherence stacks before and after trajectory compensation. Coherence matrices computed over three different land-cover types (cornfield, medium-height vegetation, and meadow) are analyzed as a preliminary assessment of the coherence behavior and temporal sampling capability of the HydroDrone system. Thermal and spatial decorrelation contributions are quantified to confirm that the observed coherence loss is primarily driven by temporal decorrelation, providing a robust experimental basis for future vegetation clutter decorrelation modeling.
author: Pietro Grassi, Marco Manzoni, Stefano Moro, Andrea Monti-Guarnieri, Julia Kubanek, Stefano Tebaldini

title: A Novel Physics-Based Empirical Line Approach for Reflectance Calibration of UAV Multispectral Imagery
content: Accurate reflectance estimation from uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery is critical for a wide range of applications and is achieved using various calibration methods. The conventional empirical line method (ELM) is a statistical digital number (DN) calibration approach that ignores input irradiance, which can introduce reflectance errors, whereas more physically accurate approaches require additional upward-looking irradiance sensors and separate calibration procedures. This study presents a novel reflectance formulation that bridges physical reflectance modeling and statistical DN calibration by reconstructing effective irradiance directly from reference panels, eliminating the need for an irradiance sensor. The method does not require additional irradiance sensors on the UAV or ground and was evaluated under variable illumination conditions. The proposed workflow first extracts raw DNs from UAV multispectral imagery together with four ground reference panels of known reflectance to establish the physical relationship between surface reflectance, radiance, and irradiance. The reference panels are measured at the start or end of the flight, or during UAV overpass acquisition. The certified spectral library of the reference calibration panels provides physically reliable reference reflectance values, which are incorporated into the radiometric model to reconstruct the effective irradiance and preserve the physical irradiance–reflectance relationship throughout the calibration process. Finally, the calibration coefficients are solved using a weighted least-squares optimization to estimate the effective irradiance. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves reflectance accuracy ( $R^{2}=0.96$ ) and robustness compared with the conventional ELM. The proposed method reduced the root mean square error (RMSE) by approximately 50% compared with the conventional ELM approach. Overall, the proposed method offers a practical calibration approach for UAV-based reflectance estimation without requiring an additional irradiance sensor.
author: Davoud Ashourloo, Daniel Smith, Lleyton Cave, Chris James, Xiaolong Chen, Sebastian Lopez-Marcano, Riku Oya, Carla Gho Brito, Andries B. Potgieter, Scott Chapman

title: MAPLE: Modality-Adaptive Prior-Guided Learning With Language-Conditioned Spatial Adaptation for Multimodal Remote Sensing Segmentation
content: Multimodal remote sensing segmentation benefits from complementary information across heterogeneous data sources, yet effectively leveraging such information while preserving the generalization ability of pretrained models remains challenging. In this article, we propose modality-adaptive prior-guided learning (MAPLE), a unified framework that adapts a frozen foundation backbone for multimodal learning via lightweight modality-aware mechanisms and language-guided priors. By introducing adaptive feature modulation and semantic guidance, the proposed approach effectively mitigates modality discrepancies and improves spatial prediction consistency. In addition, an adaptive reweighting strategy is employed to address class imbalance and enhance the learning of underrepresented categories. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that MAPLE achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with the smallest trainable footprint among the compared methods, while a comprehensive efficiency analysis of total parameters, floating-point operations (FLOPs), inference latency, and memory consumption further confirms a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off. The source code is available at https://github.com/shiroSamaNanoda/MAPLE.git
author: Qiao Sun, Zechao Hu, Lin Chen, Zerui Xiao, Shukan Liu, Hui Yang, Xianzhang Chen

title: UST-Net: Unified Spatial–Spectral–Temporal Modeling for Adaptive Hyperspectral Object Tracking
content: Hyperspectral (HS) imagery provides material-sensitive spectral cues that complement spatial appearance and improve target discrimination when red–green–blue (RGB) observations are ambiguous. Existing HS trackers have explored spectral prompting and temporal modeling, yet spectrum-preserving prompt construction, recurrent target-state propagation, and hierarchical feature adaptation remain insufficiently coordinated. We propose UST-Net, a unified spatial–spectral-- temporal framework that connects these processes within a shared transformer tracker. Its cross-modal prompt (CMP) module organizes co-registered false-color (FAC) and grouped multiband representations derived from the same HS cube into fixed-format prompts, preserving dependencies across spectral groups while accommodating different spectral configurations. The temporal state integration (TSI) module couples cross-frame Mamba hidden states with cross-stage semantic context and exchanges them with the prompt-enhanced token stream through paired injection and extraction operations. Conditioned on the resulting temporally refined tokens, the adaptive prompt injection (API) module generates stage-conditioned prompt context and applies it as residual modulation to downstream feature extraction. Experiments on the HOTC and HOT2024 datasets demonstrate that UST-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple spectral settings, with particularly strong results under occlusion and out-of-view (OV) conditions.
author: Yanni Dong, Jiaqi Zhang, Xiaole Han, Jiawei Zhou

title: ReportsNet: Rotation-Enhanced Polar-Radial Topology Synergy Network for Hyperspectral and LiDAR-Derived DSM Joint Classification
content: Joint classification of hyperspectral (HS) imagery and light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-derived digital surface models (DSMs) commonly represents local neighborhoods on Cartesian grids, where changes in object orientation alter the spatial arrangement presented to the fusion network. Existing fusion architectures do not explicitly encode center-relative radial distances, cyclic angular relationships, or geometrically corresponding cross-modal locations. To address this gap, the rotation-enhanced polar-radial topology synergy network (ReportsNet) is proposed, which locally reorganizes co-registered HS and DSM patches into target-centered polar-radial representations and models complementary distance-based and relative-angle-aware context for multimodal fusion. On the MUUFL, Trento, and Houston datasets, ReportsNet obtains OAs of 91.99%, 99.45%, and 90.69%, respectively. It achieves the highest OA on all three datasets, exceeding the next-best compared methods by 1.44, 0.44, and 1.28 percentage points, respectively. In the Houston rotation experiment from 0° to 90°, ReportsNet yields an OA standard deviation of 0.06%, indicating stable performance under the evaluated perturbations. The code is available at https://github.com/LuyangLyu/radial-flow
author: Luyang Lyu, Wenbo Yu, He Huang, Danfeng Hu, Liqiang Zhang

title: PST-DUNet: A Progressive Spectral Topology-Aware Deep Unfolding Network for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
content: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) contain rich spectral fingerprints. However, restricted by hardware bottlenecks, the acquired images often fail to satisfy the requirements for fine-grained observation. Although HSI super-resolution has achieved significant progress, many existing methods still primarily emphasize spatial detail recovery and exploit cross-band information through implicit feature interactions or output-level spectral constraints. Such a spatial-first reconstruction paradigm may provide insufficient cross-band coordination during progressive detail generation, leading to inconsistent interband response patterns and spectral distortion. To address this issue, we propose a progressive spectral topology-aware deep unfolding network (PST-DUNet). In particular, we adopt a progressive low-resolution (LR)–mid resolution (MR)–high-resolution (HR) reconstruction strategy to reduce the difficulty of direct large-scale reconstruction. In the MR stage, a parameterized observation-consistency correction is introduced to constrain the intermediate estimate with the LR observation. Meanwhile, we design an instance-adaptive dynamic spectral topology inference (DSTI) module to infer reconstruction-state-conditioned interband dependencies. Furthermore, a spectral topology rectifier (STR) is introduced to transform the topology-aggregated spectral representation into channelwise gating coefficients, thereby modulating spatial feature updates and alleviating spectral distortion. Extensive experiments on the evaluated public HSI datasets like Pavia Center, Chikusei, and CAVE demonstrate that PST-DUNet achieves superior reconstruction performance under the nonblind degradation setting, providing a favorable balance between spatial detail recovery and spectral consistency preservation.
author: Zhenyu Li, Xiangrong Zhang, Guanchun Wang, Huiyu Zhou, Xiao Han, Licheng Jiao

title: SSLANet: A Frequency–Spatial Visual System for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image classification requires a compact representation that can jointly capture discriminative spectral cues, local spatial structures, and efficient inference behavior under limited annotations. Existing CNN-based methods provide effective local pattern extraction but are less capable of modeling long-range spectral dependencies. Transformer-based models improve global interaction at the cost of considerable computational overhead, whereas recent state-space models usually formulate hyperspectral data as spatial–spectral sequences and still leave transform-domain spectral variations insufficiently explored. To address these limitations, we propose a spectral–spatial learning adaptive network (SSLANet), an efficient frequency–spatial learning network for hyperspectral image classification. The core component is a residual frequency–spatial layer that integrates an adaptive spectral block (ASB) and an interactive convolution block (ICB). ASB performs learnable complex-valued spectral modulation together with input-dependent frequency-energy selection to enhance material-sensitive spectral responses, while ICB propagates the filtered features into local neighborhoods through multiplicative spatial–channel interaction. This design differs from fixed transform-domain preprocessing in that the frequency response is conditioned on the current input feature distribution through a soft mask and an effective transfer function in the latent frequency domain. Extensive experiments on three public hyperspectral benchmarks demonstrate that SSLANet achieves competitive classification accuracy with favorable computational efficiency. The source code is available at https://github.com/NELUJA86/SSLANet
author: Xiaofei Yang, Ruiying Zhang, Weijia Cao, Jiangtao Peng, Yifang Ban, Yicong Zhou

title: A Spatial–Spectral Collaborative Method for Radiometric Cross-Calibration of Ocean Color Satellite Sensors
content: Radiometric calibration represents an indispensable foundation for quantitative ocean color remote sensing, with cross-calibration serving as a cornerstone methodology. However, existing cross-calibration methods primarily rely on linear calibration models. These approaches struggle to accurately characterize nonlinear response residuals across complex environments and overlook both the spatial correlations among adjacent pixels and the spectral correlations between distinct bands. To address these challenges, this study departs from the conventional coefficient-fitting paradigm and proposes an innovative feature-driven radiometric cross-calibration method. By learning high-dimensional image features, this approach establishes a direct sensor-to-sensor mapping, obviating the need for explicit calibration coefficients. In particular, designed for the 3-D spatial–spectral characteristics of satellite imagery, the proposed dual-branch spatial–spectral collaborative network (DB-SSCN) synergizes local spatial features and global spectral dependencies, incorporating a band-weighted loss function to balance contributions across different bands. In a case study utilizing the Chinese Ocean Color and Temperature Scanner (COCTS) onboard the Haiyang-1-D (HY-1D) satellite, the calibration results exhibit strong consistency with the standard radiance products of Aqua MODIS, yielding a mean squared error (mse) of 0.2661 and a mean relative error (MRE) of 1.18%. Furthermore, the developed algorithm demonstrates exceptional spatial and spectral preservation capabilities, achieving a structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.9879 and a spectral angle (SA) of 0.28°. The method effectively suppresses striping artifacts, thereby significantly improving the quality of the radiometric calibration products. Application experiments confirm that the method exhibits robust applicability across diverse water environments.
author: Xiaojuan Guo, Peng Ren, Yanfang Xiao, Xin Zhao, Qingjun Song, Xiaomin Ye, Keunyong Kim, Qianlong Xie, Meiyu Fan, Yi Ma, Joo-Hyung Ryu, Rongjie Liu

title: Physics-Informed Causal Heterogeneous Change Detection for Geological Disaster Assessment in Steep Mountainous Terrain
content: Heterogeneous change detection (CD) aims to detect changes between bi-temporal remote sensing images acquired with different sensors, resolutions, and radiometric properties, a critical capability for geological disaster assessment in steep mountainous terrain. However, existing methods face three intertwined challenges: cross-sensor radiometric inconsistencies that distort feature similarity, terrain-induced pseudo-changes that mask true disaster-changed areas, and error cascades in sequential registration-then-detection pipelines. To overcome these limitations, we propose PhyCDNet, a physics-driven CD framework that fuses the interpretability of radiative transfer physics with causal inference principles. By encoding the functional structure of the radiative transfer equation as learnable network layers and explicitly applying backdoor adjustment to block terrain confounding, we bridge the gap between physical priors and causal representation learning. Our approach translates a physics-constrained optimization model into a structured network comprising a cross-resolution physical manifold alignment (CRMA) module, a physics-constrained causal orthogonal decoupling (PCOD) module, and a continuous feature-flow dynamic alignment (CFDA) module. To further eliminate registration error cascades, CFDA introduces terrain-adaptive deformation constraints, while PCOD leverages orthogonality to expedite causal disentanglement. Extensive experiments on diverse datasets demonstrate that PhyCDNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on heterogeneous steep-terrain disaster scenarios. We further validate model interpretability through post-hoc radiometric compensation quality (RCQ) and terrain decoupling index (TDI) measurements, confirming that internal feature representations conform to established physical and causal priors. By integrating physics-informed causal constraints with data-driven optimization, PhyCDNet sets a new baseline for reliable and interpretable heterogeneous CD in mountainous regions. Codes are available at our Repository.
author: Zhi Li, Siying Cao, Shun Lv, Zhenming Peng, Yiguang Liu

title: FMC-DETR: Frequency-Decoupled Multidomain Coordination for Aerial-View Object Detection
content: Remote sensing object detection (RSOD) is a critical technology for real-world applications such as natural resource monitoring, traffic management, and UAV-based rescue. Detecting tiny objects in high-resolution aerial imagery remains challenging due to weak visual cues and insufficient global context modeling in complex scenes. Existing methods often suffer from delayed contextual interaction and limited nonlinear reasoning, which restrict their ability to effectively refine shallow representations and ultimately lead to suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose FMC-DETR, a frequency-decoupled fusion framework for aerial-view object detection. First, we propose the Wavelet Kolmogorov–Arnold Transformer (WeKat) backbone, which employs cascaded wavelet transforms to enhance global low-frequency structure perception in shallow features while preserving fine-grained details, and further leverages Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for adaptive nonlinear modeling of multiscale dependencies. Second, we introduce the multidomain feature coordination (MDFC) module, which refines cross-scale fused representations through partial-channel spatial, spectral, and structural coordination, thereby strengthening small-object-related feature responses in cluttered scenes. Finally, we design the compact partial fusion (CPF) module, which performs compact multibranch aggregation with progressive partial refinement to improve feature diversity and multiscale interaction while preserving stable information flow and reducing redundant perturbation. Extensive experiments across multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that FMC-DETR achieves competitive performance and consistently improves over the baseline detector. Code is available at https://github.com/bloomingvision/FMC-DETR
author: Ben Liang, Hongguang Wei, Yuan Liu, Bingwen Qiu, Yihong Wang, Xiubao Sui, Qian Chen

title: Reflected Intensity Correction Based on Global 3-D Plant Structure Acquired by Hyperspectral LiDAR
content: The precise quantification of 3-D plant biochemical parameters is essential for ecosystem assessment, yet acquiring accurate target reflectance remains a significant challenge for hyperspectral LiDAR (HSL) due to the strong incidence angle effect induced by complex leaf geometric morphology. Furthermore, existing correction methods are predominantly applied at a single-point scale rather than being strictly limited to it, struggling to accommodate the architectural complexity of whole plants. To address this bottleneck, this study proposes a novel reflectance correction framework for HSL based on the global 3-D structural information of the entire plant to suppress the effects of incidence angle on reflectance. Methodologically, an adaptive neighborhood point determination method based on point density is designed to accurately compute leaf curvature and normal vectors from point clouds, thereby avoiding over-smoothing or geometric distortion. Subsequently, a physically improved Cook–Torrance model for HSL (HSL-CT) is established to decouple diffuse and specular reflectance contributions across 28 spectral bands ranging from 445 to 810 nm. The evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed HSL-CT model consistently outperforms the baseline Lambert–Beckmann (LB) model in overall fitting accuracy and spectral fidelity. By integrating this model with the extracted global structural information, the framework effectively eliminates angular-induced specular over-brightness, significantly reduces spectral errors, and successfully restores native plant spectral signatures. Ultimately, this method can generate incidence-angle-corrected HSL reflectance data with high stability, laying a solid foundation for accurate inversion of biochemical parameters at the individual plant scale.
author: Ao Wang, Shuo Shi, Binhan Luo, Qian Xu, Xingtao Tang, Jian Yang, Ximing Ren, Chengyu Gong, Wei Gong

title: Intelligent Pre-Stack Common Offset Gather Denoising With Post-stack Structure Guidance
content: Seismic imaging is primarily used for subsurface exploration. However, the raw imaging results are often severely contaminated by various noises. To eliminate the influence of noises, various seismic denoising algorithms have been developed. Recently, deep-learning-based seismic denoising has been extensively investigated and has demonstrated significant potential. Nevertheless, most of them take only the noisy seismic image as input and directly produce the denoising output. For Pre-stack imaging gathers with extremely strong noise interference, it becomes highly challenging to discern the true structure of effective signals from the noisy input alone. This can lead denoising networks to misinterpret high-amplitude structured noise as genuine signal components, resulting in erroneous restoration. This study focuses on the Pre-stack common offset gather (COG) denoising task and proposes the prior-guided denoising (PGD) algorithm to address this challenge. The proposed PGD algorithm leverages the corresponding stacked image as a structural prior, automatically extracting guidance information to inform the denoising inference for each offset. The advantages of the proposed PGD algorithm over existing algorithms are validated through both synthetic experiments and field data applications. Field application results demonstrate that, by utilizing the stacked image as structural guidance, the PGD algorithm can restore clean single-offset images comparable in quality to Post-stack images. This not only delivers high-fidelity data for subsequent amplitude variation with offset (AVO) analysis but also enables fine-scale interpretation based on Pre-stack imaging gathers.
author: Yile Ao, Wenkai Lu, Bowu Jiang, Yonghao Wang

title: Lightweight Hierarchical Multimodal AI for Satellite-Edge Earth Observation: A Wildfire Detection Use Case
content: Satellite remote sensing provides large-area coverage for wildfire monitoring, but timely and reliable detection remains challenging because multispectral observations can be affected by smoke, haze, cloud contamination, vegetation variability, background clutter, and sensor-dependent spectral responses. At the same time, emerging low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite systems in next-generation nonterrestrial networks (NTNs) increasingly require on-board intelligence to reduce unnecessary downlink load and support low-latency Earth observation (EO) services. In this article, we propose LWHM-AI, a lightweight hierarchical multimodal AI inference framework for resource-constrained satellite-edge EO, demonstrated through a wildfire detection use case. The proposed framework combines an always-executed lightweight image-only screening model with a selectively invoked multimodal verification model through an adaptive confidence gating (ACG) policy. The first stage resolves low-uncertainty samples using down-sampled multispectral inputs, while the second stage performs compact multimodal verification for ambiguous samples by fusing full-resolution image features with auxiliary meteorological and temporal context. To select the ACG operating point, we employ a Pareto-TOPSIS-based multiobjective strategy that balances detection quality and inference cost without retraining the underlying models. The framework is evaluated on three publicly available satellite wildfire datasets, namely Landsat-8, TS-SatFire, and Sen2Fire, and compared with representative lightweight and remote-sensing-oriented baseline methods. Experimental results show that the proposed architecture achieves an average F1-score above 0.92 and an average conditional inference latency of 3.6 ms under controlled workstation profiling, demonstrating a favorable relative detection-quality versus inference-cost tradeoff for time-sensitive satellite-edge EO monitoring.
author: Sadman Sakib, Salimur Choudhury

title: Mamba-LiteDSN: Lightweight Dual-Stream Network for Efficient Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Change detection (CD) is a fundamental task in remote sensing. Many existing CD methods primarily focus on detection accuracy at the cost of a large number of parameters and high computational complexity. This article proposes a lightweight dual-stream network with Mamba for efficient remote sensing CD, named Mamba-LiteDSN. We design a dual-stream encoder–decoder architecture, in which a weight-shared MobileNetV2 encoder extracts multiscale features from bitemporal image pair. An enhanced memory visual mamba module integrates linear-complexity state-space modeling to strengthen feature representation, while a semantic-guided aggregation module (SAM) captures global semantic information from multiscale difference features. The decoder employs a channel interaction module to optimize cross-channel feature interactions and suppress pseudochanges, followed by a decoding unit (DU) that progressively restores spatial resolution under the guidance of SAM. Experiments on the public datasets LEVIR-CD and WHU-CD demonstrate that Mamba-LiteDSN achieves competitive CD performance with only 2.86 M parameters and 3.16 G FLOPs. We further construct dataset RLB-CD and evaluate the model on our custom RLB-CD dataset, verifying its effectiveness in large-scale water conservancy scenarios.
author: Wei Zhou, Zhiming Wu, Haixia Xu, Chong Yan, Siliang Zhao, Jun Zhang, Tong Yuan, Tao Yang

title: RWPNet: A Receptance Weighted Key Value Based Deep Fusion Network for Pansharpening
content: Pansharpening aims to generate high-resolution multispectral images by fusing high-resolution panchromatic (PAN) images and low-resolution multispectral images, which require simultaneously enhancing spatial details and preserving spectral information. However, most existing methods still struggle to simultaneously capture long-range spatial–spectral dependencies and effectively fuse PAN–MS features, which often lead to spatial degradation and spectral distortion. To address these issues, we propose RWPNet, a novel pansharpening network that introduces the receptance weighted key value (RWKV) mechanism. Specifically, we design the spatial–spectral RWKV (SS-RWKV) module as the core building block, which consists of a spatial–spectral integration (SSI) block and a channel refinement block. The SSI block incorporates channel WKV to capture global spectral dependencies alongside spatial modeling. To bridge global dependencies with local details, a convolutional refinement module is embedded for localized context aggregation. To effectively fuse the features from the MS and PAN branches, we develop the dual-branch cross-fusion module. This module leverages channel shuffle to strengthen interchannel feature fusion, then employs parallel SS-RWKV refinement on the mixed representations and finally performs mutual feature modulation to encourage complementary information exchange while suppressing redundant responses. The experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the superiority of RWPNet. Specifically, RWPNet achieves Q scores of 0.9149, 0.9819, and 0.9326, together with QNR scores of 0.9505, 0.9495, and 0.9530, respectively. These results demonstrate competitive performance in improving both spatial details and spectral consistency.
author: Jianwen Hu, Zhaochen Wen, Shaosheng Fan, Quan Quan

title: From Anomaly Maps to Animal Detection: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Caribou (Rangifer tarandus) Monitoring
content: Despite recent advances in supervised deep learning for wildlife detection from remote sensing imagery, annotating large-scale aerial datasets remains labor-intensive and costly, particularly in vast and heterogeneous regions such as the Arctic. Animals typically occur sparsely in background-dominated aerial imagery, which leads to consideration of animals as anomalies within unsupervised anomaly detection (AD) frameworks. However, unlike conventional AD applications, where normal samples are relatively consistent and anomalies can vary widely, aerial wildlife imagery presents a different challenge. Background, which represents the normal class, varies greatly across diverse scenes. Animals, on the other hand, exhibit consistent patterns in varied densities across terrestrial scenes. This limits the direct application of the existing AD models in wildlife detection and motivates model adaptation. In this study, the discriminatively trained reconstruction anomaly embedding model was adapted for unsupervised animal detection in large-scale Arctic aerial imagery using synthetic anomalies generated from a caribou silhouette bank constructed from a limited number of annotated samples. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed model consistently outperformed a previously adapted patch distribution model with masked autoregressive flow (PaDiM-MAF) baseline in AD, anomaly localization, and animal detection under varying background conditions and dataset complexities. Specifically, on multiherd dataset, F1-scores of 82.3%, 72.7%, and 40.9% were obtained for patch-level detection, anomaly localization, and animal detection, respectively, compared to F1 scores of 39.1%, 14.1%, and 0.6% obtained from PaDiM-MAF. While unsupervised approaches remain less effective than supervised approaches for detecting individual animals, our results show promising results in localizing animals as anomalies and motivate further investigation into their applicability for low-annotation prescreening in large-scale ecological surveys.
author: Ghazaleh Serati, Samuel Foucher, Jérôme Théau

title: MSSAM: Multiscale Spatial-Aware Mamba for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Classification
content: Applying deep learning techniques to classify multimodal remote sensing imagery plays a vital role in Earth observation. Current methods primarily face three challenges: first, interference from complex backgrounds, the presence of strongly directional structures such as roads and building clusters, and significant variations in the scale of ground objects. Second, conversely, traditional transformers are capable of modeling global dependencies, but the quadratic complexity of self-attention limits their applicability to high-resolution remote sensing data. Finally, emerging state-space models, such as Mamba, offer the advantage of linear computational complexity. However, their unidirectional scanning mechanism creates a structural contradiction with 2-D spatial understanding, leading to directional bias and contextual fragmentation. To overcome these limitations, we propose multiscale spatial-aware Mamba (MSSAM), a groundbreaking deep learning architecture that integrates the multiscale spatial-aware block, which employs a bidirectional context pre-fusion mechanism enabling a single Mamba module to capture bidirectional dependencies, and introduces dual-view Transformers to explicitly model spatial dependencies along horizontal and vertical dimensions respectively, achieving comprehensive 2-D context awareness, and the multibranch attention spectral rearrange block, which introduces a novel spectral rearrange mechanism that systematically promotes cross-branch feature interaction by reorganizing spectral features across channel groups. This enables the decoder to more effectively exploit local details and multiscale semantic information through cascaded channel and spatial attention-guided multiscale depthwise convolutions. On the Muufl, Houston, and Augsburg datasets, MSSAM achieves classification accuracies of 96.57%, 99.79%, and 97.89%, respectively, substantially outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in comprehensive evaluations. Furthermore, MSSAM exhibits superior generalization performance when tested on two single-modality datasets: Pavia University (hyperspectral) and Flevoland (PolSAR). This research introduces a novel framework for intelligent interpretation of multimodal remote sensing imagery.
author: Xiandai Cui, Li Zhang

title: Spectral Super-Resolution From RGB via Dual-Branch Feature Modeling
content: Recovering hyperspectral signals from RGB images is a severely ill-posed problem: reconstruction must preserve coherent material spectra over long spatial ranges while resolving texture-dependent variations near local structures and boundaries. Existing architectures commonly encode both regularities within a shared representation, leaving their distinct spatial requirements only implicitly coordinated. We propose SpecRINet, a dual-branch architecture in which spectral consistency flow propagates long-range material information with linear token complexity, multiscale representative region interaction captures local texture–spectrum correlations, and context-aware gating fuses the two representations according to image content. Across CAVE, Harvard, three scene-disjoint GF5A tests, and one direct cross-sensor GF5B test without fine-tuning, SpecRINet achieves the highest PSNR among the compared methods; its mean margins over the strongest competitor are 0.20 dB on CAVE, 0.63 dB on Harvard, and 0.52 dB on a held-out GF5A scene. Complementary metrics reveal scene- and sensor-dependent tradeoffs, while a boundary-conditioned diagnostic identifies residual error near material transitions.
author: KaiKai Shi, Hong Qiu, Renfang Wang, Honghui Xu, Yingying Huang, Feng Wang

title: Multidimensional Complexity Characterization With Dynamic Fusion for Infrared Ground Target Detection and Tracking
content: Quantifying infrared ground scene complexity is critical for objective algorithm evaluation, benchmark construction, and online difficulty-aware tracking analysis. This task is challenging due to time-varying interference including thermal clutter, target maneuvering, and feature degradation, while existing metrics are largely general-purpose, single-frame, or post hoc, lacking diagnostic power and failing to capture instantaneous task difficulty. We propose a multidimensional complexity characterization algorithm for infrared ground target detection and tracking, integrating three core dimensions for online, interpretable assessment. Specifically, an attention-augmented LSTM network adaptively aggregates historical motion states and quantifies motion unpredictability through normalized prediction error. A three-layer feature encoding network with hierarchical multiscale perception and cross-gated fusion extracts robust features, enabling quantification of local background suspicion and target feature degradation for low-signal-to-noise, fuzzy infrared targets through interlayer integration and reliability-aware temporal feature matching. Furthermore, a KDE-based dynamic information fusion mechanism adapts the three dimensions through statistical base weights, KDE-fitted short/full-window distributions, and a synergy matrix for interdimensional collaboration, yielding a holistic score for online difficulty assessment and failure-prone state analysis. Validated on the Anti-UAV dataset with YOLOv5 and an LCT tracker, the proposed approach generally outperforms seven comparison metrics in correlation with detection/tracking performance, trend alignment, and consistency. Cross-dataset experiments on RGB-T234 further demonstrate meaningful relationships between the proposed complexity measures and downstream performance across diverse infrared ground-target categories. This work establishes a practical foundation for difficulty-aware tracking adaptation and fair algorithm comparison, advancing infrared target detection and tracking through information fusion-driven complexity characterization.
author: Aoran Shen, Xiaotian Wang, Kun Bai, Tian Yan, Yi Wang

title: Low-Rank-Guided Tensor Mode Decoupling and Hierarchical Wavelet Synergy Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: Hyperspectral unmixing aims to separate endmember spectra from mixed pixels and estimate their abundance fractions. Despite remarkable advances in deep learning, accurately recovering fine-grained land-cover boundaries and textural details remains challenging. To this end, we propose a low-rank-guided tensor mode decoupling and hierarchical wavelet synergy network for hyperspectral unmixing, termed TMDWS-Net. First, an adaptive tensor-rank-guided denoising module employs a log-scaled adaptive rank selection module to suppress noise while preserving the stability and reliability of the 3-D spatial–spectral manifold structure. Second, a tensor mode-decoupled self-attention (TMDSA) module overcomes the limitations of conventional attention for tensor data by decoupling self-attention along the rows, columns, and spectral modes, efficiently capturing cross-band spectral correlations and global long-range spatial dependencies. To address the loss of local details, a wavelet-guided multiscale sparse cross-attention (WMSCA) module is constructed. By leveraging the multiresolution properties of the band sequential processing stationary wavelet transform and a low-frequency-guided sparse cross-attention mechanism, this module fully exploits multiscale frequency-domain structural information and selectively reinforces critical high-frequency responses, significantly enhancing the sensitivity to and representational capacity for fine-grained features. Finally, a global–local structure-aware fusion module adaptively fuses the global contextual features from the TMDSA module with the local frequency-domain detail features from the WMSCA module, achieving synergistic optimization and complementary gains between global structural information and local textural details. Experimental results on both synthetic and real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of unmixing accuracy and robustness.
author: Kewen Qu, Yuwei Wang, Chunneng Yang, Hao Wu, Wenxing Bao

title: DTDC-DeepLabv3+: A Dual-Stream Terrain-Guided Network With DenseASPP and CBAM for Water Body Extraction in Ganzhou
content: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR), an active microwave remote sensing technology with all-weather and all-time observation capability, has been widely used for water body extraction because water bodies usually exhibit low backscattering and are highly distinguishable from surrounding land covers. However, in complex mountainous environments, SAR-based water body extraction is highly susceptible to terrain-shadow interference, resulting in false extractions, discontinuities in narrow rivers, and omissions of small and scattered water bodies. To address these challenges, a dual-stream terrain-guided and densely connected atrous spatial pyramid pooling (DenseASPP) convolutional block attention module (CBAM) DeepLabv3+ model is proposed. MobileNetV2 is employed as the backbone to construct a dual-stream encoder, in which a terrain-guided module is designed to constrain SAR features using digital elevation model-derived terrain information, thereby effectively suppressing terrain-shadow-induced false extractions. In addition, DenseASPP and a strip pooling module are introduced to enhance multiscale contextual information and long-range dependencies, thereby improving the representation of continuous narrow rivers. Furthermore, a CBAM is embedded into the decoder to recalibrate fused features in both channel and spatial dimensions, enhancing the extraction of small and scattered water bodies. Experimental results in Ganzhou show that the proposed model achieves a Precision of 93.08%, a Recall of 93.36%, and a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 87.31%, outperforming commonly used semantic segmentation models, including U-Net and DeepLabv3+. The results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively suppresses terrain-shadow interference while preserving water-body structural integrity, enabling high-accuracy water body extraction in complex mountainous environments.
author: Shuhan Jia, Tiantian Gao, Quanhua Zhao, Yu Li, Xueliang Gong

title: HTFU-Net: A Cross-Modal Deep Learning Framework for Antarctic Surface Melt Mapping Using Multisource Microwave Remote Sensing Data
content: Accurate monitoring of Antarctic surface melt is essential for understanding ice-sheet mass balance and assessing future sea-level rise. Existing microwave-based melt products generally suffer from a tradeoff between spatial and temporal resolution, limiting their ability to capture both fine-scale melt patterns and continuous melt evolution. To address this challenge, this article proposes the Hierarchical Texture–Microwave Fusion U-Net (HTFU-Net), a cross-modal deep learning framework that integrates multisource microwave observations and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) texture information for Antarctic surface melt detection. The framework combines Sentinel-1-derived gray-level co-occurrence matrix texture features with advanced scatterometer backscatter observations and special sensor microwave imager/sounder brightness temperature measurements. A dual-branch encoder architecture is designed to separately learn microwave and texture representations, while a directional cross-modal attention module is introduced to intelligently bridge the datasets by dynamically identifying meaningful relationships between texture and microwave features to enhance feature interaction and adaptive fusion across modalities. Experiments conducted over representative Antarctic melt regions, including the Antarctic Peninsula, Queen Maud Land, and East Antarctic ice shelves, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 90.21%, an F1-score of 83.35%, and an intersection-over-union of 71.46%, outperforming conventional U-Net-based approaches. Results indicate that SAR texture features significantly improve melt boundary delineation and spatial consistency, while the proposed cross-modal fusion strategy enhances the detection of weak and heterogeneous melt signals. The resulting framework produces daily Antarctic surface melt maps at 500 m spatial resolution and effectively mitigates the long-standing tradeoff between spatial and temporal resolution in microwave melt monitoring. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating complementary microwave observations and SAR texture information for large-scale cryosphere monitoring and surface melt characterization.
author: Yesheng Wang, Huadong Guo, Dong Liang

title: Seamless High-Resolution Terrain Reconstruction: A Prior-Based Vision Transformer Approach
content: High-resolution elevation data is essential for hydrological modeling, hazard assessment, and environmental monitoring; however, globally consistent, fine-scale digital elevation models (DEMs) remain unavailable. Very high-resolution single-view imagery enables the extraction of topographic information at the pixel level, allowing the reconstruction of fine terrain details over large spatial extents. In this article, we present single-view-based DEM reconstruction shown to support practical analysis in GIS environments across multiple subnational jurisdictions. Specifically, we produce high-resolution DEMs for large-scale basins, representing a substantial improvement over the 30 m resolution of globally available Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) data. The DEMs are generated using a prior-based monocular depth foundation (MDE) model (PromptDA), extended in this work to the remote sensing height domain for high-resolution, globally consistent elevation reconstruction. We fine-tune the model by integrating low-resolution SRTM data as a global prior with high-resolution RGB imagery from the National Agriculture Imagery Program, producing DEMs with near light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-level accuracy. Our method achieves a $50\times$ resolution enhancement (from 30 m to 60 cm), exceeding existing super-resolution approaches by an order of magnitude. Across two diverse landscapes, the model generalizes robustly, resolving fine-scale terrain features with a mean absolute error of less than 5 m relative to LiDAR and improving upon SRTM by up to 24%. Hydrological analyses at both catchment and hillslope scales confirm the method’s utility for hazard assessment and environmental monitoring, demonstrating improved streamflow representation and catchment delineation. Finally, we demonstrate the scalability of the framework by applying it across large geographic regions.
author: Osher Rafaeli, Tal Svoray, Ariel Nahlieli

title: Wide-Swath Mapping of Antarctic Sea-Ice Height and Freeboard From SWOT Ka-Band Interferometry: Comparison Using ICESat-2
content: The surface water and ocean topography (SWOT) mission provides Ka-band wide-swath interferometric altimetry, enabling two-dimensional (2-D) observations of polar sea ice. This study presents one of the first large-scale Antarctic assessments of SWOT-derived sea-ice surface height and freeboard through near-coincident comparison with ICESat-2 laser altimetry across multiple sea-ice sectors and seasons. Sea-ice surface height relative to the DTU21 mean sea surface shows strong spatial consistency with ICESat-2 ATL07 across 130 spatiotemporally collocated regions, yielding a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.13 m and a correlation coefficient of 0.84 at 500 m resolution. SWOT-derived freeboard, retrieved using an adaptive-window inverse-distance-weighting reconstruction of the lead-referenced local sea surface, shows moderate consistency with ICESat-2 ATL10 total freeboard, with a negative bias of −0.07 m and an MAE of 0.11 m. A systematic variation of SWOT–ICESat-2 freeboard differences is observed across different freeboard regimes, with larger negative differences occurring at higher freeboard values, likely reflecting the combined effects of scale-dependent spatial representation, local sea-surface reference uncertainty, and radar–laser measurement differences. Overall, these results demonstrate that SWOT provides spatially coherent, 2-D wide-swath observations of Antarctic sea-ice freeboard, complementing the high-precision but along-track sampling of ICESat-2 and supporting improved characterization of mesoscale sea-ice variability.
author: Suhui Wu, Zhaoqing Dong, Michel Tsamados, Rosemary C. Willatt, Yao Xiao, Xiaoyi Shen, Haili Li, Hoonyol Lee, Sergey V. Popov, Chang-Qing Ke

title: A Topography-Structure-Aware and Similarity-Enhanced Network for DEM Super-Resolution
content: Digital elevation models (DEMs) are fundamental geospatial data for a wide range of applications, including engineering construction and disaster prevention. However, the spatial resolution of most existing DEM products is insufficient for refined geospatial analysis. Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) offers a promising solution for enhancing DEM resolution. Nevertheless, existing methods often overlook the guiding role of local topographic self-similarity, which contains the consistency of topographic structural morphology. Moreover, the joint learning of high- and low-frequency features tends to introduce topographic structural confusion, resulting in an imbalance between the recovery of global terrain structures and the preservation of fine details. To address these issues, this article proposes a dual-branch multiscale feature fusion network architecture, which avoids hierarchical feature interference by extracting and fusing global and local features in parallel. Within this framework, a frequency separation module is built to decouple and independently model the high- and low-frequency components of the DEM via Gaussian filtering, thus mitigating the structural confusion induced by joint frequency learning. Complementing this, the low-frequency feature adaptive modulation module leverages local topographic self-similarity and aggregates information from adjacent regions to further enhance low-frequency feature representation. Experimental results on two public DEM datasets show that, when upsampling from 30 to 10 m, the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in elevation, slope, and aspect accuracy.
author: Kaifeng Hu, Hai Xu, Yanan Liu, Weidong Yang, Xu Zou, Luxin Yan, Sheng Zhong

title: Beyond POI Categories: Confidence-Aware Multimodal Framework of Remote Sensing Images and POI Name Semantics for Urban Functional Zone Classification
content: Urban functional zone (UFZ) classification is critical for urban planning and sustainable development. Existing approaches often combine remote sensing images (RSI) with point-of-interests (POI) data. However, most POI modeling methods adopt a category-based paradigm, failing to leverage the rich semantic information contained in POI names. Moreover, most multimodal fusion strategies do not adequately consider the differences in modality confidence across individual samples. To address these issues, we propose CAM-UFZ, a confidence-aware multimodal framework that leverages RSI and POI for UFZ classification. We first introduce permutation-invariant representation learning to capture the order-invariant property of POI name sequences, generating robust semantic embeddings relevant to UFZ. To enhance multimodal discriminability, supervised multimodal contrastive learning is designed to improve intraclass compactness and interclass separability within the POI and RSI representation spaces. Furthermore, a confidence-aware fusion mechanism adaptively weights multimodal features based on their reliability, mitigating the influence of noisy or ambiguous cues. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CAM-UFZ achieves superior performance compared with other multimodal feature fusion methods. We further demonstrate the role of each strategy and provide a comprehensive analysis of the synergy mechanism between RSI and POI. Moreover, this study validates that leveraging POI name semantics is more effective than category-level features.
author: Maofan Zhao, Fujie Zhou, Qingyan Meng, Xin Tan, Alimujiang Kasimu, Shuyi Guan, Xiaowen Wang, Guoxiang Liu

title: JAD-TransUNet: A Multilevel Multimodal Semantic Segmentation Algorithm for Remote Sensing Images
content: Achieving high-precision classification of high-resolution remote sensing images is of paramount importance in the field of remote sensing research. Recently, the integration of three-band optical images [e.g., red, green, and blue (RGB) or infrared-red-green] and digital surface models (DSMs) has been extensively explored. Although the fusion of dual-source data is widely adopted, current methods continue to encounter significant challenges in practical applications. First, insufficient interaction between these two data types during feature extraction leads to difficulties in distinguishing ground objects with similar appearances, such as grass and trees. Second, simplistic reconstruction operations often result in blurred edges of objects in the output. To address these problems, a novel framework named JAD-TransUNet is proposed. Within the feature extraction stage, a Joint Cross-Squeeze-and-Excitation module is incorporated to process RGB and DSM information concurrently. This module facilitates the fusion of salient features while suppressing redundant noise, thereby enhancing feature representation accuracy. Subsequently, a specialized training scheme is developed to improve the identification of low-lying vegetation. By integrating two distinct computational methodologies, the discriminative capability for such categories is specifically strengthened. Finally, a redesigned reconstruction component is introduced using the spatially adaptive low-pass upsampling technique, which ensures image clarity and eliminates ghosting artifacts during upsampling. In addition, a local consistency optimization tool is implemented to refine object boundaries based on feature similarity. Comprehensive evaluations on two public datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across various metrics, including overall accuracy. Furthermore, experimental results confirm the efficacy of each individual component, illustrating their collective contribution to the overall performance enhancement.
author: Tingji Han, Wu Le, Zhenhong Jia, Jiajia Wang, Gang Zhou, SenSen Song, Tanghong Yuan

title: Deep Multitask Learning for Real-Time 3-D Magnetic Data Inversion With Anomaly Segmentation
content: We present a lightweight fully convolutional neural network (FCN) for 3-D inversion of magnetic data, employing a multitask learning approach to simultaneously predict voxelwise magnetic susceptibility and segment the subsurface into anomalous and nonanomalous cells. The proposed FCN framework is highly flexible and can be applied directly to various survey grid configurations and cubical mesh discretizations without modification. We train and evaluate our FCN models on a large synthetic dataset tailored for near-surface applications. On test data, our best-performing models recover over 95% of anomalous cells (within a 0.25 m spatial tolerance) with more than 96% precision, while also producing accurate susceptibility estimates. The models remain robust under noisy conditions, maintaining high performance with up to 10% Gaussian noise added to the input magnetic data. We further evaluate our model using three field surveys conducted by partners at Exodigo Inc, demonstrating that our model correctly predicts the location and shape of buried utilities.
author: R. Amzi Jeffs, Piyoosh Jaysaval, Frederick D. Day-Lewis, Aharon Joffe

title: NRMLC: A Noise-Robust Multilabel Remote Sensing Scene Classification Framework Based on Labelwise Attention and Transformer-Based Classification
content: Multilabel remote sensing scene classification (ML-RSSC) aims to assign multiple semantic labels to complex high-resolution scenes. Although exhaustive expert annotation enables accurate supervision, its high cost limits large-scale applications. Low-cost labels from crowdsourcing, existing geographic products, or weak annotation pipelines provide a scalable alternative, but they often contain missing and false-positive labels. Such noisy supervision, together with object-scale variation and severe label imbalance, makes high-precision ML-RSSC challenging. To address this issue, we propose NRMLC, a noise-robust framework for learning from low-cost noisy annotations. NRMLC first constructs multiscale scene representations through a multiscale feature extraction module to preserve objects at different spatial scales. A labelwise enhanced attention module then converts these representations into label-specific attention maps and classwise feature embeddings, alleviating the bias caused by sparse positive labels. The resulting embeddings are processed by a transformer-based multilabel classification module to model label dependencies and generate dependency-aware prediction probabilities. During optimization, a multilabel self-adaptive training strategy dynamically updates soft targets to reduce the influence of missing and false-positive annotations. Experiments on MLRSNet and UC Merced under additive, subtractive, and mixed label noise demonstrate the effectiveness of NRMLC. On MLRSNet, NRMLC reduces Hamming loss by up to 43.3% and improves mean F1 by more than 10% under challenging noisy-label settings. Ablation and probability analyses further confirm that these components jointly enhance robustness under noisy supervision.
author: Xiaoman Qi, Xingrui Zeng, Xiaotong Qi, Junhuan Peng, Yuebin Wang, Liqiang Zhang

title: Interpretable Dictionary Transfer-Based Spectral Super-Resolution for Similar-Scene Multispectral Images
content: Deep learning-based transfer learning has been widely used in spectral super-resolution, which can transfer the general spectral mapping relationship learned from a pair of multispectral (MS) and hyperspectral (HS) images to other similar-scene MS images, to realize spectral super-resolution from one single MS image to the desired HS image. However, deep learning-based transfer learning requires large amounts of data for fine-tuning and suffers from poor interpretability, which may considerably reduce the effectiveness of spectral super-resolution. To alleviate this limitation, this article proposes an interpretable dictionary transfer-based spectral super-resolution method with closed-form solutions for similar-scene multispectral images, tries to adjust the prelearned spectral dictionary to fit with different task domain and to reconstruct a more accurate desired HS image. Specifically, first, taking typical spectral set in the source domain and similar spectral set in the task domain as a connection, a transfer matrix optimization strategy is proposed for the prelearned spectral dictionary. Second, an orthogonal matrix-based dictionary transfer scheme is established, to transfer each column of the spectral dictionary prelearned from the MS and HS image pairs, into the task domain of the observed similar-scene MS image for spectral super-resolution. Finally, the coefficient matrix of the transferred spectral dictionary is optimized as closed-form solutions, by using spatial information of the observed similar-scene MS image and the spectral similarity of the extracted spectral sets under sparse and low-rank constraints. Experimental results on both simulated and real datasets indicate that, our proposed method achieves superior performance and generalization ability across different scenarios, compared with the other state-of-the-art spectral super-resolution methods based on both deep learning and dictionary learning.
author: Xiaolin Han, Jiaxun Li, Wei Wang, Huan Zhang, Lijuan Niu, Weidong Sun

title: Explicit–Implicit Collaborative Attention Guided Weakly Supervised Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
content: The task of detecting objects in remote sensing imagery is particularly challenging due to dramatic scale variability, cluttered backgrounds, and densely packed instances. To circumvent the prohibitive cost of instance-level annotation, weakly supervised object detection (WSOD) techniques that rely solely on image-level labels have attracted significant research interest. However, existing WSOD methods are prone to the part domination problem, i.e., the model overfits to the most discriminative local regions rather than the complete objects, resulting in detection accuracy significantly lower than that of fully supervised methods. To address the part domination problem, this article proposes a WSOD method for remote sensing images based on explicit–implicit collaborative attention guidance, which synergistically alleviates this problem from two levels: explicit structural design and implicit constraint learning. At the explicit level, a bottom-up aggregation attention enhancement module is designed, which integrates multilevel feature concatenation with a frequency-domain Transformer to fuse shallow spatial details and deep semantic features, thereby enhancing the positional awareness of complete objects in deep features. At the implicit level, a comprehensive attention guidance mechanism is introduced, which constructs a comprehensive attention target using attention maps from different network layers and imposes a consistency loss to force the attention maps from each perspective to approach this comprehensive target, thus suppressing the positive feedback loop of incomplete pseudolabels. Experimental results on two public remote sensing datasets, DIOR and NWPU VHR-10.v2, show that the proposed method achieves mean average precision of 30.82% and 72.24%, respectively, outperforming existing mainstream WSOD methods and effectively alleviating the part domination problem.
author: Yueyi Han, Weida Zhan, Dehua Huo, Yong Tian, Xiaoyu Xu, Depeng Zhu, Kaibo Zhang, Jingru Feng

title: Enhancing High Spatial Resolution SAR-to-Optical Image Translation via Wavelet-Derived Multiscale Features Over Croplands
content: High spatial resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is often acquired in single-polarization modes, which inherently limits its capacity to reconstruct the spectral characteristics of optical imagery in deep learning-based SAR-to-optical (S2O) image translation. To address this limitation, this study investigates the effects of wavelet-derived multiscale features on S2O image translation and evaluates their potential to enhance information representation in single-polarization SAR imagery. Pix2Pix and a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (cDDPM) are implemented, and three input configurations are compared: original SAR imagery alone, wavelet-derived features alone, and a combination of both. Five wavelet basis functions, including Haar, Daubechies 4 (Db4), Symlets 4 (Sym4), Coiflets 4, and Biorthogonal 4.4, are analyzed using COSMO-SkyMed SAR and PlanetScope optical imagery at a spatial resolution of 3 m acquired over croplands in Gimje, South Korea. The results show that incorporating wavelet-derived multiscale features improves reconstruction performance, with more pronounced improvements for Pix2Pix. When SAR imagery exhibits greater local variation, features extracted using the Haar basis function enhance structural boundary information, leading to improved structural reconstruction in Pix2Pix. In contrast, the Db4 and Sym4 basis functions, owing to their symmetry and smoothness, show relatively robust performance across acquisition dates and are more suitable for cDDPM under different temporal conditions. These findings suggest that extracting wavelet-derived multiscale features from single-polarization SAR imagery is effective for high spatial resolution S2O image translation and highlight the importance of selecting an appropriate wavelet basis function based on SAR image characteristics, input configuration, and the deep learning model used.
author: Soyeon Park, No-Wook Park

title: Continuous Phase Reconstruction in Two Stages and Global Graph Optimization for InSAR Deformation Monitoring Over Large Areas
content: InSAR phase unwrapping is essential for recovering continuous surface deformation from interferometric measurements, but strong noise, low coherence, and steep phase gradients can cause ambiguity errors and error propagation. Large interferograms introduce an additional challenge because tile based inference may produce scale differences, inconsistent phase references, seams, and low frequency drift. To address these problems, this study proposes a two stage continuous phase reconstruction framework combined with global graph optimization. In the first stage, a multiscale encoder decoder network integrates sine and cosine representations, local wrapped phase differences, and coherence information to recover a denoised wrapped phase. A coherence weighted periodic consistency loss is used to suppress noise while maintaining fringe continuity. In the second stage, the continuous phase is decomposed into a normalized spatial pattern and a global scale factor, which are estimated by separate branches and constrained by pattern, scale, phase, local difference, and rewrapping losses. The two stages are trained progressively and subsequently refined jointly. For large scene processing, relative scale and offset constraints are derived from overlapping tiles and solved globally using sparse weighted least squares. Coherence modulated feather blending is then applied to obtain a spatially continuous phase field. Experiments on simulated and real InSAR data demonstrate improved robustness in noisy, low coherence, and high gradient regions, with fewer local unwrapping errors, tile seams, and long wavelength drift. For an 8192 × 8192 interferogram, the total processing time was 43.84 s, of which graph optimization and blending accounted for only 4.4%.
